national/agency: DESIGNATED AGENCY IS PRESUMED: a licensee working with a person represents that person unless a WRITTEN AGREEMENT says otherwise or the licensee performs ONLY MINISTERIAL ACTS (La. R.S. 9:3892).
WHO PAYS DOES NOT DECIDE WHO IS REPRESENTED - payment or promise of payment is not determinative of agency (La. R.S. 9:3896).
CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION NEVER includes material information about the PHYSICAL CONDITION of the property (La. R.S. 9:3891(6)(b)).
A Louisiana DUAL AGENT MUST DISCLOSE the buyer's or tenant's FINANCIAL QUALIFICATION to the seller or landlord, and all LATENT MATERIAL DEFECTS known (La. R.S. 9:3897(A)).
A licensee selling property HE OWNS is NOT a dual agent, and a licensee-landlord on a lease of three years or less is not either (La. R.S. 9:3891(10), 9:3897(G)).
THE CLIENT IS NOT VICARIOUSLY LIABLE for the licensee's acts or omissions (La. R.S. 9:3899).
SUBAGENCY requires a WRITTEN AGREEMENT; MLS membership never creates it (La. R.S. 9:3898).
No agency disclosure is required for a LEASE OF THREE YEARS OR LESS with no contemplated sale (La. R.S. 9:3893(F)).
national/disclosures: PSYCHOLOGICALLY IMPACTED PROPERTY - a HOMICIDE, OTHER FELONY OR SUICIDE on the property, or an occupant's HIV or AIDS status - IS NOT a material fact or material defect, and no cause of action arises from not disclosing it (La. R.S. 37:1468).

EVERY written residential lease and sale contract executed by a licensee must contain the STATEWIDE SEX OFFENDER DATABASE NOTICE with its phone number and internet site; delivering it discharges any further duty on offender proximity (La. R.S. 37:1469).

The MOLD INFORMATIONAL PAMPHLET, if delivered, goes AT OR BEFORE the lease or contract, and then no further mold information is required - but it never alters the duty to disclose a KNOWN MATERIAL DEFECT (La. R.S. 37:1470).
Failure to provide the WRITTEN RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY DISCLOSURE FORM under La. R.S. 9:3196 et seq. is an express ground for discipline (La. R.S. 37:1455(A)(33)).
At the time an offer is presented the licensee must tell BOTH parties that each may owe certain costs AND THEIR APPROXIMATE AMOUNT (La. R.S. 37:1455(A)(25)).
NON-CASH earnest money is allowed only if the owner is told BEFORE acceptance AND the fact appears ON THE FACE of the purchase agreement (La. R.S. 37:1455(A)(24)).

Louisiana is a CIVIL LAW state: REDHIBITION replaces the implied warranty of quality, LESION BEYOND MOIETY lets a seller rescind a sale under half of fair market value, and a sum given is a DEPOSIT unless EARNEST MONEY is stipulated - in which case a receding seller owes it back DOUBLE (CC 2520, 2589, 2624).
national/practice: Louisiana mandates the COMMISSION'S PRESCRIBED PURCHASE AGREEMENT FORM for 1-4 unit residential offers, and NO PERSON MAY ALTER IT - addenda only (La. R.S. 37:1449.1).
ERRORS AND OMISSIONS INSURANCE IS MANDATORY for every active licensee (La. R.S. 37:1466).
NET LISTINGS ARE UNLAWFUL for residential property or land, and a broker may not even ADVISE OR ENCOURAGE one (La. R.S. 37:1448.3).

Education: 90 HOURS prelicence, then 45 POST-LICENCE HOURS WITHIN 180 DAYS, then 12 HOURS A YEAR of continuing education with 4 mandatory; a broker needs FOUR YEARS licensed and 150 hours (La. R.S. 37:1437).
Licences run ONE YEAR, renew BY SEPTEMBER 30, EXPIRE DECEMBER 31, with a delinquent window closing DECEMBER 31 (La. R.S. 37:1442).
Records are kept FIVE YEARS, copies go to a signing principal IMMEDIATELY and to all signers WITHIN FIVE DAYS of the final signature (La. R.S. 37:1449).

The RECOVERY FUND pays only $20,000 per claim and per transaction, $50,000 per licensee, must be claimed WITHIN 180 DAYS of final judgment, and PAYMENT AUTOMATICALLY REVOKES the licence (La. R.S. 37:1462, 37:1463).
A SINGLE unlicensed act violates the chapter, at up to $500 PER DAY from five days after the cease-and-desist letter (La. R.S. 37:1436).
The Commission has ELEVEN members, all brokers of at least five years' standing, with a QUORUM OF SIX (La. R.S. 37:1432, 37:1433).

pass_note: Louisiana reports a SCALED score from 0 to 100 and sets the salesperson passing score at 70 on the national portion and 70 on the state portion, graded separately. Brokers and prelicensing instructors need 75 on each portion. Numeric scores are reported only to failing candidates.

la/agency.blurb: Designated agency, ministerial acts, confidential information, dual agency, vicarious liability.
examples: A licensee meets a buyer at an open house, answers questions about the house, and sets a showing appointment. Nothing is signed. Who does the licensee represent?

Those are all ministerial acts, so the designated agency presumption has not attached. But the moment the conversation reaches the buyer's financing or motives - substantive contact - the licensee is presumed to represent that buyer as a designated agent unless there is a written agreement saying otherwise (La. R.S. 9:3891(12), (14), 9:3892).
A dual agent knows the buyer is barely qualified and the seller asks about it.

The dual agent MUST disclose the buyer's financial qualification to the seller - the statutory form lists it as something a dual agent shall do. What the dual agent may not reveal is the price either side would accept or pay, or other confidential information, without permission (La. R.S. 9:3897(A), (B)).
The seller refuses to consent to a dual agency when an in-house buyer appears.

The licensee may withdraw from representing the non-consenting client without liability, keep representing the other client in that transaction, and still represent the withdrawing client in other transactions. A referral fee for sending that client elsewhere needs written disclosure to both clients (La. R.S. 9:3897(F)).
A client is sued because their agent misrepresented the lot size.

Under La. R.S. 9:3899 the client is not liable for the licensee's acts or omissions in providing brokerage services. The licensee's own duty as to negligent or fraudulent misrepresentation is unaffected (La. R.S. 9:3893(E)).

l: NOTWITHSTANDING Civil Code Articles 2985 through 3032 OR ANY OTHER LAW, a licensee engaged in any real estate transaction SHALL BE CONSIDERED TO BE REPRESENTING THE PERSON WITH WHOM HE IS WORKING AS A DESIGNATED AGENT - unless there is a WRITTEN AGREEMENT between the broker and the person providing a different relationship, OR the licensee is performing ONLY MINISTERIAL ACTS (9:3892).

"DESIGNATED AGENCY" is defined as the agency relationship that SHALL BE PRESUMED TO EXIST when a licensee working with a client is engaged in any real estate transaction, unless a written agreement provides for a different relationship (9:3891(8)).
A "DESIGNATED AGENT" is simply a licensee who is the agent of a client (9:3891(9)).

So the default in Louisiana runs the OPPOSITE WAY from states where an unrepresented person is a customer until they sign something. Here the licensee represents the person unless a writing or ministerial-acts-only status says otherwise.

"CLIENT" means one who engages the professional advice and services of a licensee as his agent. "CUSTOMER" means a person who is NOT being represented by a licensee BUT FOR WHOM THE LICENSEE IS PERFORMING MINISTERIAL ACTS (9:3891(4), (7)).
"AGENCY" means a relationship in which a broker or licensee represents a client BY THE CLIENT'S CONSENT, WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, in an IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TRANSACTION (9:3891(1)).
A "BROKERAGE AGREEMENT" is an agreement for brokerage services provided to a person in return for compensation or the right to receive compensation from another (9:3891(3)).
THE PAYMENT OR PROMISE OF PAYMENT OF COMPENSATION TO A BROKER IS NOT DETERMINATIVE of whether an agency relationship has been created (9:3896). Who pays does not decide who is represented.
AGENCY DISCLOSURE IS NOT REQUIRED for a lease that does NOT EXCEED A TERM OF THREE YEARS and under which NO SALE of the property to the lessee is contemplated (9:3893(F)).

l: MINISTERIAL ACTS are those acts a licensee may perform for a person that are INFORMATIVE IN NATURE. Performing only ministerial acts is what keeps the designated agency presumption from attaching.

The statute's examples, which are NOT EXHAUSTIVE: RESPONDING TO PHONE INQUIRIES about the availability and pricing of brokerage services; RESPONDING TO PHONE INQUIRIES about the price or location of property; CONDUCTING AN OPEN HOUSE and answering questions about the property; SETTING AN APPOINTMENT TO VIEW PROPERTY.

Also ministerial: RESPONDING TO QUESTIONS from persons WALKING INTO the licensee's office about brokerage services or particular properties; ACCOMPANYING AN APPRAISER, INSPECTOR, CONTRACTOR or similar third party on a visit; DESCRIBING A PROPERTY OR ITS CONDITION in response to an inquiry.

Also ministerial: COMPLETING BUSINESS OR FACTUAL INFORMATION for a person REPRESENTED BY ANOTHER LICENSEE on an offer or contract to purchase; SHOWING A PERSON THROUGH A PROPERTY BEING SOLD BY AN OWNER ON HIS OWN BEHALF; and REFERRAL to another broker or service provider.

"SUBSTANTIVE CONTACT" is THAT POINT IN ANY CONVERSATION WHERE CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION IS SOLICITED OR RECEIVED. It includes any SPECIFIC FINANCIAL QUALIFICATIONS of the consumer, or the MOTIVES OR OBJECTIVES the consumer may divulge, which if disclosed to the other party COULD HARM THE PARTY'S BARGAINING POSITION. It INCLUDES ANY ELECTRONIC CONTACT, ELECTRONIC MAIL OR OTHER ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION (9:3891(14)).

The line to hold: answering factual questions is ministerial; the moment the conversation turns to what the person can afford or why they are moving, it is SUBSTANTIVE CONTACT and the relationship question has to be settled.

IT STOPS BEING CONFIDENTIAL if any of three things happens: THE CLIENT PERMITS THE DISCLOSURE BY WORD OR CONDUCT; THE DISCLOSURE IS REQUIRED BY LAW OR WOULD REVEAL A SERIOUS DEFECT; or THE INFORMATION BECOMES PUBLIC FROM A SOURCE OTHER THAN THE LICENSEE.
CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION SHALL NOT BE CONSIDERED TO INCLUDE MATERIAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE PHYSICAL CONDITION OF THE PROPERTY. A client cannot make a defect confidential by asking.
Confidential information CAN BE DISCLOSED BY A DESIGNATED AGENT TO HIS BROKER for the purpose of SEEKING ADVICE OR ASSISTANCE FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE CLIENT.

l: A licensee REPRESENTING A CLIENT shall: PERFORM THE TERMS OF THE BROKERAGE AGREEMENT; PROMOTE THE BEST INTERESTS OF THE CLIENT; and EXERCISE REASONABLE SKILL AND CARE in performing brokerage services.

Promoting the client's best interests means THREE things: SEEKING A TRANSACTION at the price and terms stated in the brokerage agreement or otherwise acceptable to the client; TIMELY PRESENTING ALL OFFERS TO AND FROM THE CLIENT; and TIMELY ACCOUNTING for all money and property in which the client has, may have, or should have had an interest.

A licensee DOES NOT BREACH a duty by SHOWING ALTERNATIVE PROPERTIES to prospective buyers or tenants, or by showing properties the client is interested in TO OTHER prospective buyers or tenants (9:3893(B)).
A licensee representing a BUYER OR TENANT does NOT breach a duty BY WORKING ON THE BASIS THAT THE LICENSEE SHALL RECEIVE A HIGHER FEE BASED ON A HIGHER SELLING PRICE (9:3893(C)).
A licensee is NOT LIABLE TO A CLIENT for providing FALSE INFORMATION that was provided to the licensee BY A CUSTOMER, UNLESS the licensee KNEW OR SHOULD HAVE KNOWN it was false (9:3893(D)).
Nothing in the section changes a licensee's legal duty as to NEGLIGENT OR FRAUDULENT MISREPRESENTATION of material information (9:3893(E)).

TO CUSTOMERS: licensees SHALL TREAT ALL CUSTOMERS HONESTLY AND FAIRLY and, when representing a client, may assist a customer by PERFORMING MINISTERIAL ACTS. Doing so shall NOT be construed to violate the brokerage agreement with the client, and shall NOT be construed to FORM A BROKERAGE AGREEMENT WITH THE CUSTOMER (9:3894(A)).

A licensee is NOT LIABLE TO A CUSTOMER for false information given to the customer if the information came FROM THE LICENSEE'S CLIENT OR THE CLIENT'S AGENT and the licensee DID NOT HAVE ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE that it was false (9:3894(B)). Note the asymmetry: for a CLIENT the test is knew OR SHOULD HAVE KNOWN; for a CUSTOMER it is ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE.

l: DUAL AGENCY means a licensee working with BOTH BUYER AND SELLER, or BOTH LANDLORD AND TENANT, in the same transaction (9:3891(10)).

IT IS NOT DUAL AGENCY if the licensee IS THE SELLER OF PROPERTY HE OWNS, or if the property is owned by a REAL ESTATE BUSINESS OF WHICH THE LICENSEE IS THE SOLE PROPRIETOR AND AGENT. Nor is it dual agency where the licensee is working with both landlord and tenant on a LEASE NOT EXCEEDING THREE YEARS AND THE LICENSEE IS THE LANDLORD (9:3891(10), 9:3897(G)).

A licensee may act as a dual agent ONLY WITH THE INFORMED WRITTEN CONSENT OF ALL CLIENTS. INFORMED CONSENT IS PRESUMED to have been given by any client WHO SIGNS A DUAL AGENCY DISCLOSURE FORM PREPARED BY THE COMMISSION (9:3897(A)).

WHAT A DUAL AGENT SHALL DO, in the statutory form's own words: TREAT ALL CLIENTS HONESTLY; PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT THE PROPERTY to the buyer or tenant; DISCLOSE ALL LATENT MATERIAL DEFECTS IN THE PROPERTY KNOWN TO THE LICENSEE; DISCLOSE THE FINANCIAL QUALIFICATION OF THE BUYER OR TENANT TO THE SELLER OR LANDLORD; EXPLAIN REAL ESTATE TERMS; HELP THE BUYER OR TENANT ARRANGE PROPERTY INSPECTIONS; EXPLAIN CLOSING COSTS AND PROCEDURES; HELP THE BUYER COMPARE FINANCING ALTERNATIVES; and PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT COMPARABLE PROPERTIES THAT HAVE SOLD so both clients can make educated decisions on price.

WHAT A DUAL AGENT SHALL NOT DISCLOSE: CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION about either client without that client's permission; THE PRICE THE SELLER OR LANDLORD WILL TAKE OTHER THAN THE LISTING PRICE without permission; and THE PRICE THE BUYER OR TENANT IS WILLING TO PAY without permission (9:3897(B)).
TIMING: the written consent must be obtained AT THE TIME THE BROKERAGE AGREEMENT IS ENTERED INTO OR AT ANY TIME BEFORE THE LICENSEE ACTS AS A DUAL AGENT (9:3897(C)).
NO CAUSE OF ACTION arises against a dual agent for making disclosures ALLOWED OR REQUIRED by the section, and making them DOES NOT TERMINATE ANY AGENCY RELATIONSHIP (9:3897(D)).

NO IMPUTATION: in dual agency, EACH CLIENT AND LICENSEE POSSESS ONLY ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE AND INFORMATION. There is NO IMPUTATION of knowledge or information AMONG OR BETWEEN THE CLIENTS, BROKERS, OR THEIR AFFILIATED LICENSEES (9:3897(E)).

WITHDRAWAL: a licensee may WITHOUT LIABILITY WITHDRAW from representing a client WHO HAS NOT CONSENTED to a disclosed dual agency. The withdrawal does NOT prejudice the licensee's ability to keep representing the other client in that transaction, or to represent the withdrawing client in other transactions. On withdrawal the licensee SHALL NOT RECEIVE A REFERRAL FEE for referring that client to another licensee UNLESS WRITTEN DISCLOSURE IS MADE TO BOTH the withdrawing client and the client who continues to be represented (9:3897(F)).

SUBAGENCY CAN ONLY BE CREATED BY A WRITTEN AGREEMENT. A licensee is NOT a subagent SOLELY BY REASON OF MEMBERSHIP OR OTHER AFFILIATION BY THE BROKER IN A MULTIPLE LISTING SERVICE or other similar information source (9:3898).

vocab: Designated agency
The agency relationship presumed to exist when a licensee works with a client, unless a written agreement provides otherwise (La. R.S. 9:3891(8), 9:3892).
Ministerial acts
Informative acts a licensee may perform for a person without creating agency - answering factual questions, holding an open house, setting appointments, making referrals (La. R.S. 9:3891(12)).
Substantive contact
The point in a conversation, including electronic contact, where confidential information is solicited or received (La. R.S. 9:3891(14)).
Confidential information
Client information made confidential in writing by the client, or whose disclosure could materially harm the client - never including the property's physical condition (La. R.S. 9:3891(6)).
Customer
A person not represented by the licensee, for whom the licensee performs ministerial acts, owed honest and fair treatment (La. R.S. 9:3891(7), 9:3894).
Vicarious liability
The liability Louisiana abolished: a client is not liable for the acts or omissions of a licensee providing brokerage services for the client (La. R.S. 9:3899).

la/civillaw.blurb: Immovables, ownership, servitudes, usufruct, community property, successions, obligations, sales, leases.
examples: A seller sells a lot worth $200,000 for $90,000 and later regrets it.

The price is less than half the fair market value, so the seller may seek rescission for lesion beyond moiety. Only the seller can claim it, only for corporeal immovables, not in a court-ordered sale - and he may invoke it even if he renounced the right (CC 2589).
A purchase agreement says the buyer gives $10,000 and calls it nothing in particular. The buyer walks away.

By default that sum is a DEPOSIT on account of the price, not earnest money, so the buyer does not buy a right to recede. Had the parties stipulated earnest money, the buyer would forfeit it - and a seller who receded would owe it back plus an equal amount (CC 2624).
Eighteen months after closing, a buyer discovers the slab is cracked. The seller did not know.

The redhibition action against a seller who did not know prescribes two years from delivery OR one year from discovery, whichever comes first - so the buyer has a year from discovery, inside the two years from delivery. The buyer must also give the seller timely notice so repairs can be attempted (CC 2520, 2522, 2534(A)).
A one-year residential lease ends and the tenant stays nine days with no word from either side.
The lease is reconducted: for a fixed term longer than a week, remaining in possession one week without notice to vacate or other opposition reconducts it on the same terms (CC 2721(2)).

l: TRACTS OF LAND, WITH THEIR COMPONENT PARTS, ARE IMMOVABLES (CC 462). Louisiana says "immovable", not "real property".

COMPONENT PARTS of a tract of land are BUILDINGS, OTHER CONSTRUCTIONS PERMANENTLY ATTACHED TO THE GROUND, STANDING TIMBER, AND UNHARVESTED CROPS OR UNGATHERED FRUITS OF TREES - WHEN THEY BELONG TO THE OWNER OF THE GROUND (CC 463).

BUILDINGS AND STANDING TIMBER ARE SEPARATE IMMOVABLES WHEN THEY BELONG TO A PERSON OTHER THAN THE OWNER OF THE GROUND (CC 464). This is the Louisiana answer to the question of who owns a building on leased land.
CORPOREAL MOVABLES are things, ANIMATE OR INANIMATE, that NORMALLY MOVE OR CAN BE MOVED from one place to another (CC 471).
ALL THINGS, CORPOREAL OR INCORPOREAL, THAT THE LAW DOES NOT CONSIDER AS IMMOVABLES, ARE MOVABLES (CC 475). Movable is the residual category.
A thing is CORPOREAL if it has a body and can be felt; INCORPOREAL if it is a right - so a servitude or a usufruct is an incorporeal immovable.

LEGAL DESCRIPTIONS: Louisiana land is described by PARISH (not county), and much of the state outside the original French and Spanish grants is on the GOVERNMENT RECTANGULAR SURVEY, while older tracts use metes and bounds and ARPENT measurements along the rivers.

l: ONE MAY HAVE VARIOUS RIGHTS IN THINGS: OWNERSHIP; PERSONAL AND PREDIAL SERVITUDES; AND SUCH OTHER REAL RIGHTS AS THE LAW ALLOWS (CC 476).

OWNERSHIP IS THE RIGHT THAT CONFERS ON A PERSON DIRECT, IMMEDIATE AND EXCLUSIVE AUTHORITY OVER A THING. The owner MAY USE, ENJOY AND DISPOSE OF IT within the limits and under the conditions established by law (CC 477).

OWNERSHIP OF THE SAME THING BY TWO OR MORE PERSONS IS OWNERSHIP IN INDIVISION. Absent other law or juridical act, THE SHARES OF ALL CO-OWNERS ARE PRESUMED TO BE EQUAL (CC 797). Louisiana says "indivision", not "tenancy in common".
SUBSTANTIAL ALTERATIONS OR IMPROVEMENTS to a thing held in indivision require the consent of all co-owners (CC 804).

USUFRUCT IS A REAL RIGHT OF LIMITED DURATION ON THE PROPERTY OF ANOTHER. Its features vary with whether the things are CONSUMABLES OR NONCONSUMABLES (CC 535). The usufruct is Louisiana's answer to the life estate; the person who owns the thing subject to it is the NAKED OWNER.

If the things are NONCONSUMABLES, the USUFRUCTUARY has the right to POSSESS THEM AND DERIVE THE UTILITY, PROFITS AND ADVANTAGES they produce, UNDER THE OBLIGATION OF PRESERVING THEIR SUBSTANCE. He must USE THEM AS A PRUDENT ADMINISTRATOR and DELIVER THEM TO THE NAKED OWNER at the termination of the usufruct (CC 539).

A usufructuary MAY NOT dispose of nonconsumable things unless expressly granted the right - though he MAY dispose of corporeal movables GRADUALLY AND SUBSTANTIALLY IMPAIRED BY USE, WEAR OR DECAY, such as equipment, appliances and vehicles, acting as a prudent administrator (CC 568).

USUFRUCT MAY BE ESTABLISHED BY A JURIDICAL ACT INTER VIVOS OR MORTIS CAUSA, OR BY OPERATION OF LAW. One created by juridical act is CONVENTIONAL; one created by operation of law is LEGAL. It may be established on ALL KINDS OF THINGS, movable or immovable, corporeal or incorporeal (CC 544).
THE RIGHT OF USUFRUCT EXPIRES UPON THE DEATH OF THE USUFRUCTUARY (CC 607).

HABITATION and RIGHT OF USE are the other PERSONAL SERVITUDES: habitation is the right to dwell in the house of another, and right of use confers a specified limited advantage over the property of another.

l: A PREDIAL SERVITUDE IS A CHARGE ON A SERVIENT ESTATE FOR THE BENEFIT OF A DOMINANT ESTATE. THE TWO ESTATES MUST BELONG TO DIFFERENT OWNERS (CC 646). This is Louisiana's easement.

PREDIAL SERVITUDES MAY BE NATURAL, LEGAL, AND VOLUNTARY OR CONVENTIONAL. NATURAL servitudes arise from the NATURAL SITUATION OF ESTATES; LEGAL servitudes are IMPOSED BY LAW; and VOLUNTARY OR CONVENTIONAL servitudes are established by JURIDICAL ACT, PRESCRIPTION, OR DESTINATION OF THE OWNER (CC 654).
PREDIAL SERVITUDES ARE ESTABLISHED ON, OR FOR THE BENEFIT OF, DISTINCT CORPOREAL IMMOVABLES (CC 698).
Their USE AND EXTENT are regulated by THE TITLE BY WHICH THEY ARE CREATED, and in the absence of such regulation, by the Code's default rules (CC 697).

THE SERVITUDE OF PASSAGE is the right for the dominant estate's benefit whereby PERSONS, ANIMALS, UTILITIES OR VEHICLES may pass through the servient estate. Unless the title says otherwise, the EXTENT AND MODE must be SUITABLE FOR THE KIND OF TRAFFIC OR UTILITY NECESSARY FOR THE REASONABLE USE of the dominant estate (CC 705).

BUILDING RESTRICTIONS are CHARGES IMPOSED BY THE OWNER OF AN IMMOVABLE IN PURSUANCE OF A GENERAL PLAN governing BUILDING STANDARDS, SPECIFIED USES AND IMPROVEMENTS. THE PLAN MUST BE FEASIBLE AND CAPABLE OF BEING PRESERVED (CC 775). These are Louisiana's restrictive covenants.
Building restrictions MAY BE ESTABLISHED ONLY BY JURIDICAL ACT EXECUTED BY THE OWNER of an immovable OR BY ALL THE OWNERS of the affected immovables (CC 776).

They MAY IMPOSE AFFIRMATIVE DUTIES that are REASONABLE AND NECESSARY FOR THE MAINTENANCE OF THE GENERAL PLAN - but they MAY NOT impose on an owner or his successors THE OBLIGATION TO PAY A FEE OR OTHER CHARGE ON THE OCCASION OF AN ALIENATION, LEASE OR ENCUMBRANCE of the immovable (CC 778). That last clause outlaws private transfer fees.

l: COMMUNITY PROPERTY comprises: property acquired DURING THE EXISTENCE OF THE LEGAL REGIME THROUGH THE EFFORT, SKILL OR INDUSTRY OF EITHER SPOUSE; property acquired WITH COMMUNITY THINGS or with community and separate things unless classified separate under CC 2341; property DONATED TO THE SPOUSES JOINTLY; NATURAL AND CIVIL FRUITS OF COMMUNITY PROPERTY; DAMAGES AWARDED FOR LOSS OR INJURY TO A COMMUNITY THING; AND ALL OTHER PROPERTY NOT CLASSIFIED BY LAW AS SEPARATE (CC 2338).

THINGS IN THE POSSESSION OF A SPOUSE during the existence of a regime of COMMUNITY OF ACQUETS AND GAINS ARE PRESUMED TO BE COMMUNITY, but either spouse MAY PROVE THAT THEY ARE SEPARATE PROPERTY (CC 2340). The presumption is the practical rule a licensee meets at the listing table.

SEPARATE PROPERTY of a spouse IS HIS EXCLUSIVELY and comprises: property acquired BEFORE the community regime was established; property acquired WITH SEPARATE THINGS, or with separate and community things WHERE THE COMMUNITY PORTION IS INCONSEQUENTIAL in comparison; property acquired BY INHERITANCE OR DONATION TO HIM INDIVIDUALLY; damages awarded in an action for BREACH OF CONTRACT AGAINST THE OTHER SPOUSE or for loss from the other spouse's FRAUD OR BAD FAITH IN MANAGING COMMUNITY PROPERTY; damages connected with MANAGING HIS SEPARATE PROPERTY; and things acquired through a VOLUNTARY PARTITION of the community during the regime (CC 2341).

USUFRUCT OF THE SURVIVING SPOUSE: IF THE DECEASED SPOUSE IS SURVIVED BY DESCENDANTS, THE SURVIVING SPOUSE SHALL HAVE A USUFRUCT OVER THE DECEDENT'S SHARE OF THE COMMUNITY PROPERTY to the extent the decedent has NOT DISPOSED OF IT BY TESTAMENT. THIS USUFRUCT TERMINATES WHEN THE SURVIVING SPOUSE DIES OR REMARRIES, WHICHEVER OCCURS FIRST (CC 890).

SUCCESSIONS vocabulary: a succession is TESTATE where the decedent left a valid testament and INTESTATE where he did not. Heirs who cannot be deprived of their share are FORCED HEIRS, and the share the law reserves to them is the LEGITIME. A usufruct over the legitime in favour of the surviving spouse is a PERMISSIBLE BURDEN that does not impinge on the legitime.
DONATIONS transfer ownership gratuitously - INTER VIVOS during life, MORTIS CAUSA by testament.

EMINENT DOMAIN appears in Louisiana as EXPROPRIATION, and APPROPRIATION is the taking of property for public use by certain bodies without prior judicial proceedings; the Louisiana Constitution limits taking for "public purpose".

sections.h: Obligations, sales and the authentic act (CC 1833, 1839, 2456, 2589, 2624)
l: AN AUTHENTIC ACT is a writing EXECUTED BEFORE A NOTARY PUBLIC or other authorised officer, IN THE PRESENCE OF TWO WITNESSES, and SIGNED BY EACH PARTY who executed it, BY EACH WITNESS, AND BY EACH NOTARY before whom it was executed. Each signer's name must be TYPED OR HAND-PRINTED LEGIBLY IMMEDIATELY BENEATH THE SIGNATURE (CC 1833(A)).

The writing NEED NOT BE EXECUTED AT ONE TIME OR PLACE, or before the same notary or the same witnesses, so long as each party signs before a notary and two witnesses and all sign. FAILURE TO INCLUDE THE TYPED OR PRINTED NAMES DOES NOT AFFECT VALIDITY OR AUTHENTICITY. If a party cannot sign, the notary must cause him to AFFIX HIS MARK (CC 1833(B), (C)).

A TRANSFER OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY MUST BE MADE BY AUTHENTIC ACT OR BY ACT UNDER PRIVATE SIGNATURE. Nevertheless an ORAL TRANSFER IS VALID BETWEEN THE PARTIES when the property HAS BEEN ACTUALLY DELIVERED AND THE TRANSFEROR RECOGNISES THE TRANSFER WHEN INTERROGATED ON OATH (CC 1839).

THE REGISTRY RULE: an instrument involving immovable property SHALL HAVE EFFECT AGAINST THIRD PERSONS ONLY FROM THE TIME IT IS FILED FOR REGISTRY IN THE PARISH WHERE THE PROPERTY IS LOCATED (CC 1839). Louisiana's race-to-the-courthouse rule - unrecorded rights simply do not exist as to third parties.

OWNERSHIP IS TRANSFERRED BETWEEN THE PARTIES AS SOON AS THERE IS AGREEMENT ON THE THING AND THE PRICE IS FIXED, EVEN THOUGH THE THING SOLD IS NOT YET DELIVERED NOR THE PRICE PAID (CC 2456). Delivery of an immovable is deemed to take place on execution of the writing that transfers ownership (CC 2477).

LESION BEYOND MOIETY: THE SALE OF AN IMMOVABLE MAY BE RESCINDED FOR LESION WHEN THE PRICE IS LESS THAN ONE HALF OF THE FAIR MARKET VALUE of the immovable. LESION CAN BE CLAIMED ONLY BY THE SELLER and only in sales of CORPOREAL IMMOVABLES. IT CANNOT BE ALLEGED IN A SALE MADE BY ORDER OF THE COURT. THE SELLER MAY INVOKE LESION EVEN IF HE HAS RENOUNCED THE RIGHT TO CLAIM IT (CC 2589).

DEPOSIT VERSUS EARNEST MONEY: a sum given by the buyer to the seller in connection with a contract to sell IS REGARDED AS A DEPOSIT ON ACCOUNT OF THE PRICE UNLESS THE PARTIES HAVE EXPRESSLY PROVIDED OTHERWISE. IF the parties STIPULATE THAT IT IS EARNEST MONEY, EITHER PARTY MAY RECEDE from the contract - but THE BUYER WHO RECEDES MUST FORFEIT THE EARNEST MONEY, AND THE SELLER WHO RECEDES MUST RETURN IT PLUS AN EQUAL AMOUNT. Where earnest money has been given and a party fails to perform for reasons other than a FORTUITOUS EVENT, that party is REGARDED AS RECEDING from the contract (CC 2624).
So the default is a DEPOSIT, which does not buy a right to walk away; EARNEST MONEY is an opt-in that buys both sides a priced exit. This distinction is heavily tested.

l: THE SELLER WARRANTS THE BUYER AGAINST REDHIBITORY DEFECTS, OR VICES, IN THE THING SOLD. A defect is REDHIBITORY when it RENDERS THE THING USELESS, or its use SO INCONVENIENT that it must be presumed the buyer WOULD NOT HAVE BOUGHT it had he known - which gives the buyer the right to obtain RESCISSION. A defect is ALSO redhibitory when, WITHOUT RENDERING THE THING TOTALLY USELESS, it DIMINISHES ITS USEFULNESS OR VALUE so that the buyer WOULD STILL HAVE BOUGHT IT BUT FOR A LESSER PRICE - which limits him to a REDUCTION OF THE PRICE (CC 2520).
NO WARRANTY is owed for defects THAT WERE KNOWN TO THE BUYER at the time of the sale, or FOR DEFECTS THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN DISCOVERED BY A REASONABLY PRUDENT BUYER of such things (CC 2521).

THE BUYER MUST GIVE THE SELLER NOTICE of a redhibitory defect, SUFFICIENTLY TIMELY TO ALLOW THE SELLER THE OPPORTUNITY TO MAKE THE REQUIRED REPAIRS. A buyer who fails to do so SUFFERS DIMINUTION OF THE WARRANTY to the extent the seller shows the defect could have been repaired, or repaired less burdensomely, with timely notice. NOTICE IS NOT REQUIRED WHERE THE SELLER HAS ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE of the defect (CC 2522).

PRESCRIPTION OF THE REDHIBITION ACTION: against a seller WHO DID NOT KNOW of the defect, it prescribes in TWO YEARS FROM THE DAY OF DELIVERY to the buyer OR ONE YEAR FROM THE DAY THE DEFECT WAS DISCOVERED by the buyer, WHICHEVER OCCURS FIRST. Against a seller WHO KNEW OR IS PRESUMED TO HAVE KNOWN, it prescribes in ONE YEAR FROM DISCOVERY OR TEN YEARS FROM THE PERFECTION OF THE CONTRACT, WHICHEVER OCCURS FIRST. Prescription is INTERRUPTED when the seller ACCEPTS THE THING FOR REPAIRS and begins anew when he TENDERS IT BACK or NOTIFIES THE BUYER OF HIS REFUSAL OR INABILITY to repair (CC 2534).

THE WARRANTY MAY BE EXCLUDED OR LIMITED BY AGREEMENT, but the terms MUST BE CLEAR AND UNAMBIGUOUS AND MUST BE BROUGHT TO THE ATTENTION OF THE BUYER. A buyer IS NOT BOUND by an otherwise effective exclusion WHEN THE SELLER HAS DECLARED THAT THE THING HAS A QUALITY HE KNEW IT DID NOT HAVE. The buyer is SUBROGATED to the seller's warranty rights against other persons even when the warranty is excluded (CC 2548).

ACQUISITIVE PRESCRIPTION: OWNERSHIP AND OTHER REAL RIGHTS IN IMMOVABLES MAY BE ACQUIRED BY THE PRESCRIPTION OF TEN YEARS (CC 3473). The REQUISITES are POSSESSION OF TEN YEARS, GOOD FAITH, JUST TITLE, AND A THING SUSCEPTIBLE OF ACQUISITION BY PRESCRIPTION (CC 3475).

OWNERSHIP AND OTHER REAL RIGHTS IN IMMOVABLES MAY ALSO BE ACQUIRED BY THE PRESCRIPTION OF THIRTY YEARS WITHOUT THE NEED OF JUST TITLE OR POSSESSION IN GOOD FAITH (CC 3486). So: TEN YEARS WITH good faith and just title, THIRTY YEARS WITHOUT.

RECONDUCTION: a LEASE WITH A FIXED TERM IS RECONDUCTED if, after the term expires and WITHOUT NOTICE TO VACATE OR TERMINATE or other opposition by lessor or lessee, the LESSEE REMAINS IN POSSESSION - FOR THIRTY DAYS in the case of an AGRICULTURAL LEASE; FOR ONE WEEK for other leases with a fixed term LONGER THAN A WEEK; and FOR ONE DAY for a lease with a fixed term EQUAL TO OR SHORTER THAN A WEEK (CC 2721). Reconduction continues the lease on the same terms, not a holdover tenancy at sufferance.

Leases may be VERBAL OR WRITTEN in Louisiana. EVICTION procedure is statutory, and RESIDENTIAL SECURITY DEPOSITS are governed by La. R.S. 9:3251 et seq., which requires the lessor to return the deposit or give an itemised statement of retentions WITHIN ONE MONTH after the lease ends.

la/civillaw.summary: Fourteen items, and nothing here carries over from a common-law state. Louisiana has IMMOVABLES not real property, USUFRUCT not life estates, PREDIAL SERVITUDES not easements, COMMUNITY PROPERTY, LESION BEYOND MOIETY, REDHIBITION and RECONDUCTION. Learn the vocabulary first.
traps: IMMOVABLE, not real property. MOVABLE, not personal property. PARISH, not county.
USUFRUCT is not a life estate and the other side is the NAKED OWNER. It ends at the usufructuary's death.
PREDIAL SERVITUDE needs TWO ESTATES WITH DIFFERENT OWNERS.
LESION BEYOND MOIETY: price under HALF of fair market value, SELLER only, corporeal immovables only, and a renunciation does not bar it.
A sum given is a DEPOSIT by default. EARNEST MONEY must be stipulated, and then the seller who backs out pays DOUBLE.
Redhibition prescribes 2 years from delivery / 1 year from discovery against an innocent seller; 1 year from discovery / 10 years from the contract against a knowing one.
Acquisitive prescription: TEN years WITH good faith and just title, THIRTY years WITHOUT.
RECONDUCTION renews the lease on the same terms - one week for ordinary fixed-term leases, thirty days for agricultural.
Recording is what makes an instrument effective AGAINST THIRD PERSONS.
vocab: Immovable
Louisiana's category for land, its component parts, and buildings or standing timber owned separately from the ground (CC 462-464).
Usufruct / naked owner
The real right of limited duration to use and enjoy another's property, and the person who owns the thing subject to it (CC 535, 539).
Predial servitude
A charge on a servient estate for the benefit of a dominant estate owned by someone else - Louisiana's easement (CC 646).
Building restrictions
Charges imposed by an owner under a feasible general plan governing standards, uses and improvements; no transfer fees allowed (CC 775, 778).
Ownership in indivision
Ownership of one thing by two or more persons, shares presumed equal (CC 797).
Community of acquets and gains
Louisiana's default marital regime, under which things in a spouse's possession are presumed community (CC 2338, 2340).
Lesion beyond moiety
The seller's right to rescind a sale of a corporeal immovable sold for less than half its fair market value (CC 2589).
Redhibition
The buyer's action for rescission or price reduction for a hidden defect in the thing sold (CC 2520).
Authentic act
A writing executed before a notary and two witnesses and signed by all of them and the parties (CC 1833).
Reconduction
The automatic continuation of a fixed-term lease when the lessee stays on without opposition (CC 2721).
Bond for deed
A Louisiana contract to sell in which the price is paid in instalments and the deed is delivered on full payment (La. R.S. 9:2941 et seq.).
Acquisitive prescription
Acquiring ownership of an immovable by possession - ten years with good faith and just title, thirty years without (CC 3473, 3475, 3486).

l: The Louisiana Real Estate Commission is created WITHIN THE OFFICE OF THE GOVERNOR and consists of ELEVEN MEMBERS APPOINTED BY THE GOVERNOR. ONE member comes from EACH OF THE SEVEN SUPREME COURT DISTRICTS, TWO are appointed AT LARGE, and TWO more are appointed from specified congressional-district pairings. EACH APPOINTMENT GOES TO THE SENATE FOR CONFIRMATION (37:1432(A)).

Each appointment is for a FOUR-YEAR TERM. NO COMMISSIONER MAY SERVE MORE THAN TWO FOUR-YEAR TERMS CONSECUTIVELY, and after two consecutive terms a person is not eligible again UNTIL FOUR YEARS from the last date served (37:1432(B)).

Members must be CITIZENS AND QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF LOUISIANA, and EACH MEMBER MUST HAVE ACTIVELY ENGAGED IN THE REAL ESTATE BUSINESS AS A BROKER FOR AT LEAST FIVE YEARS immediately preceding appointment (37:1432(C)). There is no consumer-member seat.
A vacancy other than by expiration of term is filled by the GOVERNOR FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE UNEXPIRED TERM, and the GOVERNOR MAY REMOVE ANY MEMBER FOR CAUSE (37:1432(D), (E)).
The Commission ELECTS A CHAIRMAN AND A SECRETARY FROM ITS MEMBERS and SELECTS A VICE CHAIRMAN to serve in the chairman's absence (37:1433(A)).

SIX MEMBERS CONSTITUTE A QUORUM for all business. The Commission MEETS QUARTERLY OR MORE OFTEN if necessary, is LIMITED TO TWO REGULARLY SCHEDULED MEETINGS PER MONTH, and ADDITIONAL MEETINGS MAY BE CALLED ON APPLICATION OF THREE MEMBERS (37:1433(B)).

Members are compensated at NOT MORE THAN FIFTY DOLLARS A DAY per meeting or for attending to Commission business, with no double payment for two meetings on the same day, plus actual expenses (37:1433(C)).
The Commission APPOINTS AN EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR with the powers it delegates, sets the salary, and MAY REMOVE THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR CAUSE (37:1435(G)).

The grounds run to THIRTY-SIX numbered items and include: violating the License Law or any Commission rule; violating the LOUISIANA TIMESHARING ACT; FAILURE TO ACCOUNT for money belonging to others; FAILURE TO PROPERLY DISBURSE such money; COMMINGLING; and accepting, giving or charging any UNDISCLOSED COMMISSION, REBATE OR DIRECT PROFIT on expenditures made for a principal.

Also: CONVICTION OF A FELONY or a plea of GUILTY OR NOLO CONTENDERE to a felony charge (37:1455(A)(29)); PROCURING A LICENCE by fraud, misrepresentation or deceit (A)(31); ENGAGING IN REAL ESTATE ACTIVITY DURING A SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION (A)(34); and USING ADVERTISING THAT IS MISLEADING OR INACCURATE (A)(35).

Also: HAVING BEEN FINALLY ADJUDICATED AND FOUND GUILTY of refusing, BECAUSE OF RACE, COLOR, NATIONAL ORIGIN, SEX OR ETHNIC GROUP, to show, sell or rent real estate to qualified purchasers or renters, or of ANY VIOLATION OF THE FAIR HOUSING ACT OF 1968 OR THE LOUISIANA EQUAL HOUSING OPPORTUNITY ACT (37:1455(A)(28)).
Also: ENGAGING IN ANY EFFORT, INCLUDING THE REFERRAL OR RECOMMENDATION OF A SPECIFIC HOME INSPECTOR, WITH THE INTENT TO DECEIVE OR DEFRAUD (37:1455(A)(36)).

sections.h: The Real Estate Recovery Fund (37:1461 to 37:1463)
l: The LOUISIANA REAL ESTATE RECOVERY FUND reimburses any person ADJUDGED TO HAVE SUFFERED MONETARY DAMAGES by reason of ANY VIOLATION OF THE LICENSE LAW, or of OBTAINING MONEY OR PROPERTY BY FRAUD, MISREPRESENTATION, DECEIT, FALSE PRETENSES, ARTIFICE OR TRICKERY, committed as part of a transaction involving the SALE OR LEASE OF REAL PROPERTY IN THIS STATE by a broker or salesperson WHO WAS LICENSED AT THE TIME (37:1461(A)).

The Commission SHALL MAINTAIN A MINIMUM LEVEL OF FOUR HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS for recovery and guaranty purposes, and may invest the fund under the same limitations as other state funds (37:1461(C)). Surplus above the $400,000 minimum MAY BE TRANSFERRED on 31 December each year to the RESEARCH AND EDUCATION FUND (37:1461(B)(4), 37:1464).

CONDITIONS FOR RECOVERY: the claimant must have a FINAL JUDGMENT in a Louisiana court on a cause of action BASED ON A VIOLATION OF THE CHAPTER; must have GIVEN NOTICE OF THE ACTION TO THE COMMISSION BY CERTIFIED MAIL when the action was commenced (on which the Commission MAY INTERVENE AND DEFEND IN THE DEFENDANT'S NAME); must have MADE THE JUDGMENT EXECUTORY with a sheriff's or constable's return showing NO PROPERTY CAN BE FOUND or that the sale proceeds were INSUFFICIENT; and must have made ALL REASONABLE SEARCHES AND INQUIRIES for assets (37:1462(A)).

The claimant must have DILIGENTLY PURSUED REMEDIES AGAINST ALL JUDGMENT DEBTORS AND ALL PERSONS LIABLE. Where the claim rests on the acts of a CORPORATION, PARTNERSHIP OR LLC, the claimant MUST HAVE DILIGENTLY PURSUED ALL POSSIBLE REMEDIES AGAINST THE QUALIFYING BROKER for that entity. If the debtor sought BANKRUPTCY protection, the claimant must provide a STAMPED COPY OF THE PROOF OF CLAIM filed in that case (37:1462(A)(1)(d)).

THE DEADLINE: the right to recovery is FOREVER BARRED unless application is made WITHIN ONE HUNDRED EIGHTY DAYS from the date of the FINAL JUDGMENT OF ALL JUDICIAL PROCEEDINGS, INCLUDING APPEALS (37:1462(A)(1)(f)).
CONSENT JUDGMENTS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE for payment UNLESS the Commission has INTERVENED in the lawsuit and is a party to the consent judgment (37:1462(A)(2)).

THE AFFIDAVIT ROUTE: in lieu of the full conditions, the Commission may allow a claim submitted BY NOTARISED AFFIDAVIT where the claim is based on licensees SANCTIONED BY THE COMMISSION in an adjudicatory proceeding whose record CORROBORATES the affidavit, AND THE CLAIM DOES NOT EXCEED TWO THOUSAND DOLLARS - with the same 180-day bar running from the effective date of the Commission's order (37:1462(B)).

THE CAPS: payment equals the UNSATISFIED PORTION OF THE JUDGMENT OR TWENTY THOUSAND DOLLARS, WHICHEVER IS LESS, and only to the extent the judgment reflects ACTUAL DAMAGES. Payments for claims ARISING OUT OF THE SAME TRANSACTION are limited IN THE AGGREGATE TO TWENTY THOUSAND DOLLARS regardless of the number of claimants or parcels. Payments against ANY ONE LICENSEE SHALL NOT EXCEED FIFTY THOUSAND DOLLARS IN THE AGGREGATE (37:1463(A), (C), (D)).

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LICENSEE: upon payment of ANY AMOUNT from the fund in settlement of a claim or satisfaction of a judgment against a licensed broker or salesperson, THAT LICENCE IS AUTOMATICALLY REVOKED. A DISCHARGE OF BANKRUPTCY SHALL NOT RELIEVE a person from these penalties and disabilities (37:1463(G)).

Recovery fund: $20,000 per claim AND per transaction, $50,000 per licensee. Much lower than most states.
Payment from the fund AUTOMATICALLY REVOKES the licence, and bankruptcy does not undo that.
180 DAYS from final judgment to apply - one of the shortest windows in the country.
Record inspection happens 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on business days.

The fund that reimburses actual damages from a licensee's License Law violation or fraud, capped at $20,000 per transaction and $50,000 per licensee (La. R.S. 37:1461-1463).
Qualifying broker
The broker designated for an entity, against whom a recovery fund claimant must have diligently pursued all possible remedies (La. R.S. 37:1462(A)(1)(d)(ii)).
Executory judgment
A judgment made enforceable, with a sheriff's return showing no property can be found - a precondition to recovery fund payment (La. R.S. 37:1462(A)(1)(c)).

The fund that may receive the recovery fund's surplus above its $400,000 minimum each 31 December (La. R.S. 37:1461(B)(4), 37:1464).

FAILURE TO TIMELY COMPLETE CONTINUING EDUCATION IS A VIOLATION OF THE CHAPTER (37:1437(C)(5)(a)).

CLOSING COSTS: FAILURE TO INFORM THE BUYER AND SELLER, AT THE TIME AN OFFER IS PRESENTED, that either party may be expected to pay certain costs such as discount points, AND THE APPROXIMATE AMOUNT of those costs, is a ground for discipline (37:1455(A)(25)).

MISREPRESENTING THE PRICE: representing to any LENDER, GUARANTEEING AGENCY or other interested party, verbally or through FALSE DOCUMENTS, AN AMOUNT IN EXCESS OF THE TRUE AND ACTUAL SALE PRICE, or terms differing from those actually agreed, is a ground for discipline (37:1455(A)(18)).
GUARANTEEING FUTURE PROFITS which may result from the resale of real property, or authorising anyone to guarantee them, is a ground for discipline (37:1455(A)(10)).

l: RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY DISCLOSURE: FAILURE BY A LICENSEE TO PROVIDE A BUYER OR SELLER WITH A WRITTEN PROPERTY DISCLOSURE FORM for sales and certain leases involving RESIDENTIAL REAL PROPERTY, pursuant to LA. R.S. 9:3196 ET SEQ., is a ground for discipline (37:1455(A)(33)).

KNOWN MATERIAL DEFECTS: FAILURE TO DISCLOSE TO A BUYER A KNOWN MATERIAL DEFECT regarding the condition of real estate of which the broker, salesperson or timeshare interest salesperson HAS KNOWLEDGE is a ground for discipline (37:1455(A)(27)).

PSYCHOLOGICALLY IMPACTED PROPERTY (37:1468): the fact or SUSPICION that a property is psychologically impacted - including that an occupant is or was suspected to be infected with HIV or diagnosed with AIDS, or any other disease medically determined to be HIGHLY UNLIKELY TO BE TRANSMITTED THROUGH OCCUPANCY of a dwelling; or that the property WAS OR WAS SUSPECTED TO HAVE BEEN THE SITE OF A HOMICIDE, OTHER FELONY, OR A SUICIDE - IS NOT A MATERIAL FACT OR MATERIAL DEFECT that must be disclosed.
NO CAUSE OF ACTION arises against an owner or his agent for FAILURE TO DISCLOSE that the property was psychologically impacted (37:1468(B)).

OFFENDER NOTIFICATION (37:1469): EVERY written lease or rental agreement executed by a licensee for RESIDENTIAL IMMOVABLE PROPERTY, and EVERY written contract for the SALE of residential immovable property, SHALL CONTAIN A NOTICE of the availability of public access to the STATEWIDE DATABASE disclosing the locations of registered offenders, INCLUDING THE TELEPHONE NUMBER AND INTERNET SITE.

On delivery of that notice, the lessor, seller, broker or licensee IS NOT REQUIRED TO PROVIDE ANY ADDITIONAL INFORMATION about the proximity of registered sex offenders; the notice IS DEEMED ADEQUATE, and gives rise to NO CAUSE OF ACTION against the disclosing party (37:1469(B)).

MOLD PAMPHLET (37:1470): the Commission approves a MOLD INFORMATIONAL PAMPHLET which MAY be distributed to buyers. IF the licensee delivers it, he must do so AT OR BEFORE the time a lease, rental agreement or contract for sale is entered into; the licensee is then NOT REQUIRED TO PROVIDE ANY ADDITIONAL INFORMATION about mold, and the pamphlet IS DEEMED ADEQUATE.

A licensee IS NOT LIABLE for an error, inaccuracy or omission in the mold pamphlet if it was NOT WITHIN HIS PERSONAL KNOWLEDGE, or was based on information from the Commission, a public agency or an expert's report where the licensee EXERCISED ORDINARY CARE in obtaining and transmitting it (37:1470(C)). Nothing in the section ALTERS THE DUTY TO DISCLOSE ANY KNOWN MATERIAL DEFECT (37:1470(D)).

ADVERTISING: USING ADVERTISING THAT IS MISLEADING OR INACCURATE is a ground for discipline (37:1455(A)(35)). REPRESENTING OR ATTEMPTING TO REPRESENT a broker or agency OTHER THAN THE LICENSED BROKER OR AGENCY LISTED ON THE LICENCE issued by the Commission is another (37:1455(A)(8)).
KNOWINGLY MAKING ANY FALSE REPRESENTATIONS to any party in a real estate transaction is a ground for discipline (37:1455(A)(15)).

la/statutory.summary: Fourteen items on the mechanics: Louisiana's PRESCRIBED purchase agreement form that may not be altered, compensation only from the sponsoring broker, five-year record retention, and a long list of prohibited acts.
traps: The Commission's PURCHASE AGREEMENT FORM is mandatory for 1-4 unit residential offers and MAY NOT BE ALTERED. Addenda are fine.
Copies: IMMEDIATELY to the signing principal, and within FIVE DAYS of the final signature for multi-party documents.
Records: FIVE years, and going inactive does not end the duty.
NET LISTINGS are unlawful - a broker may not even advise or encourage one.
A licensee accepts compensation ONLY from their sponsoring or qualifying broker.
Non-cash earnest money is allowed only if told to the owner BEFORE acceptance AND shown on the face of the agreement.
Psychologically impacted property - homicide, felony, suicide, HIV or AIDS - is NOT a disclosable material fact in Louisiana.
The offender-database notice must be IN every written residential lease and sale contract.
vocab: Prescribed purchase agreement form
The Commission's residential purchase agreement form, mandatory for 1-4 unit residential offers and not alterable (La. R.S. 37:1449.1).
Net listing
A listing promising the seller a net return and letting the licensee keep the excess - unlawful in Louisiana for residential property or land (La. R.S. 37:1448.3).
Buyer agreement
The written agreement a broker must execute with a buyer, stating the compensation or how it is calculated (La. R.S. 37:1448.4).
Psychologically impacted property
Property affected by a homicide, felony, suicide, or an occupant's HIV or AIDS status - expressly not a material fact in Louisiana (La. R.S. 37:1468).
Reasonable cause

The precondition for lawfully seeking a referral fee: having introduced the client or holding a written referral contract, and receiving the referral before the client contracted (La. R.S. 37:1447(A)).
